bib.title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

question: Can retrieval-augmented generation of existing JSON steps and table names reduce hallucination and allow a smaller LLM in a natural-language-to-workflow (structured output) task?
hypothesis: Suggesting retrieved step and table names in the LLM prompt reduces hallucinated steps/tables, generalises to out-of-domain deployments without retraining, and lets a small LLM plus a small retriever match a larger LLM.
contributions: We provide an application of RAG in workflow generation, a structured output task.
We show that using RAG reduces hallucination and improves results.
We demonstrate that RAG allows deploying a smaller LLM while using a very small retriever model, at no loss in performance.

method.summary: A siamese 110M sentence encoder is fine-tuned with contrastive loss to map natural-language requirements to JSON workflow step and table objects; a FAISS index returns top-K suggestions that are prepended to the prompt of a LoRA-fine-tuned code LLM (StarCoderBase 1B-15.5B, CodeLlama-7B, Mistral-7B) that generates the workflow JSON with greedy decoding. Retriever and LLM are trained separately.
method.task: natural language to workflow JSON generation (structured output) with retrieval of steps and tables

datasets.name: In-domain workflows (Train)
datasets.source: around 4,000 deployed workflows from internal deployments with annotator-written requirements, plus around 1,000 deterministic simple samples (internal, not released)
datasets.preprocessing: Most frequent steps excluded from retriever suggestions; in training the retriever is assumed 100% recall (needed steps/table always in suggestions). Retriever pairs: around 15,000 step pairs and 1,500 table pairs

datasets.name: Human Eval
datasets.source: expert users simulating interaction through a UI; used for final metrics

datasets.name: OOD1-OOD5
datasets.split: five splits from other deployments; % steps not in Train: 49%, 76%, 34%, 33%, 7%
datasets.source: real workflows from other deployments, annotator-written requirements

models.name: all-mpnet-base-v2 (fine-tuned)
models.architecture: siamese transformer encoder, mean pooling, L2 normalisation

training.objective: LLM: supervised fine-tuning with retriever suggestions in prompt; retriever: contrastive loss L = 1/2 [Y D^2 + (1-Y) max(0, 1/2 - D)^2], D = 1 - cossim; negatives random, BM25 or ANCE

other.retriever_hardware: inferred: not stated; only LLM hardware given

inference.samples: inferred: single greedy generation per item; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: short simple format: suggested tables and steps (JSON) before the user query, then expected output (Fig 3)
inference.retrieval: FAISS index of steps and tables, cosine similarity, top K; eval Recall@15 for steps, Recall@10 for tables; K used in the LLM prompt not stated

metrics.name: Trigger Exact Match
metrics.definition: generated JSON trigger identical to ground truth, including table name if required

metrics.name: Bag of Steps
metrics.definition: order-agnostic overlap between generated and ground-truth steps

metrics.name: Hallucinated Steps / Tables
metrics.definition: % of generated steps/tables per workflow that do not exist

metrics.name: Recall@15 (steps), Recall@10 (tables)
metrics.definition: top-K retrieved set covers the steps and table in the reference JSON

baselines: RAG-trained model run without suggestions on OOD
eval.protocol: Single runs on Human Eval and OOD splits, no seeds or significance tests; OOD average weighted by samples per split.

availability.data: internal enterprise data, not stated as released

results.claim: Without a retriever, fine-tuned StarCoderBase-1B hallucinates 19.2% of tables on Human Eval.
results.setup: Human Eval, StarCoderBase-1B, no retriever vs with retriever (0.044)
results.table: Table 4, row No Retriever StarCoderBase-1B, column Hallucinated Tables (0.192); with retriever 0.044

results.claim: Retriever cuts hallucinated steps for StarCoderBase-7B from 0.137 to 0.019 on Human Eval.
results.setup: Human Eval, StarCoderBase-7B, LoRA fine-tuned, greedy
results.table: Table 4, row With Retriever StarCoderBase-7B, column Hallucinated Steps (0.019); no retriever 0.137

results.claim: Without retriever, hallucinated steps and tables reach up to 21% on Human Eval; with retriever below 7.5% steps and 4.5% tables for StarCoderBase models.
results.quote: the % of hal- lucinated steps and tables can be as high as 21% on the "Human Eval" split
results.note: The 21% is the table rate of StarCoderBase-3B (0.214).

results.claim: Fine-tuning the 110M encoder with all negative strategies gives Step Recall@15 of 0.743 vs 0.425 for the base all-mpnet-base-v2.
results.setup: Human Eval, all-mpnet-base-v2 + All negatives (random, BM25, ANCE)
results.table: Table 3, row + All, column Step Recall@15 (0.743); all-mpnet-base-v2 0.425

results.claim: Table Recall@10 rises from 0.170 to 0.766 after fine-tuning with all negatives.
results.table: Table 3, row + All, column Table Recall@10 (0.766)

results.claim: Scaling off-the-shelf GTR-T5 encoders does not significantly improve retrieval (best step recall 0.579 for 1.24B).
results.quote: Scaling the size of the off-the-shelf encoders, as we did with GTR-T5, does not yield significant improvements

results.claim: RAG fine-tuned 3B is competitive with 15.5B without RAG on Trigger EM and Bag of Steps while hallucination stays low.
results.setup: Human Eval, StarCoderBase-3B with retriever vs 15.5B no retriever
results.table: Table 4, row With Retriever StarCoderBase-3B Trigger EM 0.615 vs No Retriever StarCoderBase (15.5B) 0.632
results.note: Bag of Steps 0.641 vs 0.662; the 3B is lower on both metrics, so 'competitive' not 'equal'.

results.claim: StarCoderBase-7B with retriever is the chosen trade-off: Trigger EM 0.664, BofS 0.672 versus 15.5B 0.667 / 0.667.
results.table: Table 4, row With Retriever StarCoderBase-7B, column Trigger EM

results.claim: CodeLlama-7B and Mistral-7B with RAG are worse than StarCoderBase-7B across all metrics.
results.setup: Human Eval, with retriever, CodeLlama-7B vs StarCoderBase-7B
results.table: Table 4, row With Retriever CodeLlama-7B, column Hallucinated Tables (0.108)
results.note: Authors suspect natural-language pretraining is detrimental; untested.

results.claim: On five OOD splits, weighted-average hallucinated steps with RAG is 0.018 versus 0.020 without suggestions, but hallucinated tables is 0.066 versus 0.428.
results.setup: RAG fine-tuned StarCoderBase-7B on OOD1-5 without further fine-tuning; baseline is same model with suggestions removed
results.table: Table 5, rows Avg. and No RAG Avg., column HT (0.066 vs 0.428)
results.note: n = sum of OOD sizes (146+162+429+42+353), inferred.

results.claim: OOD average Trigger EM 0.647 and BofS 0.714 with suggestions, vs 0.544 and 0.629 without.
results.table: Table 5, rows Avg. and No RAG Avg., column Trigger EM

results.claim: Without suggestions, the RAG-trained model hallucinated steps stay roughly the same because it learned to be conservative and reuse seen steps.
results.table: Table 6, row OOD1 (40% no suggestions, 13% with suggestions)
results.note: Per-workflow rate (Table 5) is similar, unique-name rate differs.

limits: Datasets are internal (ServiceNow), mostly IT domain, and not released; no code or weights stated.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; Human Eval only 157 examples.
Retriever and LLM trained separately; joint training not tried. In training retriever recall assumed 100%, a mismatch with inference.
Retrieval errors and LLM structure errors (IF, TRY, FOREACH) remain; more than 10% of unique steps still invented in some OOD splits.
Most frequent steps are excluded from suggestions and memorised, so hallucination of common steps is not retrieval-controlled.
No comparison against guided/grammar-constrained generation; latency numbers not reported.
Authors do not claim hallucination risk eliminated; deployed system post-processes to flag nonexistent steps.
Explanation for CodeLlama/Mistral underperformance is a suspicion only.
